content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "High frequency of CT/MRI scans",
      "quote": "CT/MRI | X | X",
      "page": 52,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "CT/MRI scans are scheduled every 4 months for the first two years and every 6 months in year 3, which is frequent and burdensome for patients, especially in a neoadjuvant setting where imaging is also needed for response assessment.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing imaging frequency to every 6 months in years 1-2, or align with standard of care."
    },
    {
      "title": "ADA sample not collected in year 3",
      "quote": "ADA Sample | X |",
      "page": 52,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The ADA sample is only collected in years 1-2, but immunogenicity monitoring should continue throughout the treatment period, including year 3, to capture late-onset ADA responses.",
      "fix": "Add ADA sample collection to year 3 visits."
    },
    {
      "title": "TSH reflex testing may cause extra visits",
      "quote": "TSH (with reflex T3, free T4) | X | X",
      "page": 52,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Reflex testing for T3 and free T4 may lead to additional blood draws or unscheduled visits if abnormal TSH results require confirmation, increasing patient burden.",
      "fix": "Specify that reflex testing is only performed if TSH is abnormal, and consider using a single sample for all thyroid tests."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs windows too tight",
      "quote": "The allowable window for each specified time point is ±10 minutes.",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "9.2.3.1 Vital Signs",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "A ±10 minute window for post-infusion vital signs is very tight and may be difficult to meet in a busy clinical setting, especially when infusions run long or other procedures are scheduled concurrently.",
      "fix": "Widen the window to ±15 or ±20 minutes to reduce site burden and patient waiting."
    },
    {
      "title": "ECG parameters not fully specified",
      "quote": "The following will be recorded on the eCRF: • RR interval (sec) • PR interval (msec) • QRS interval (msec) • QT interval (msec) • Heart rate (beats per minute; recorded from the ventricular rate)",
      "page": 60,
      "section": "9.2.3.3 Electrocardiogram",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The ECG section does not mention QTc (corrected QT) interval, which is a standard parameter for oncology trials and important for cardiac safety monitoring.",
      "fix": "Add QTc interval (e.g., QTcF) to the list of ECG parameters to be recorded."
    },
    {
      "title": "PRO frequency not specified in schedule",
      "quote": "Patient reported outcomes will be measured at a frequency indicated in Table 2 and Table 3 using the self-administered EORTC QLQ-C30.",
      "page": 65,
      "section": "9.2.9 Patient Reported Outcomes",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The text refers to Table 2 and Table 3 for frequency, but the provided Schedule of Activities (page 52) does not include a row for PROs, making it unclear how often patients will complete the questionnaire.",
      "fix": "Add a PRO row to the Schedule of Activities with clear frequency (e.g., every cycle or every 4 months)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Screening labs must be done within 72 hours of first dose",
      "quote": "Serum ß-HCG (test must be done ≤72 hours before the first dose)",
      "page": 54,
      "section": "9.2.1 Procedures Performed Only at the Screening/Baseline Visit",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring serum ß-HCG within 72 hours before first dose may force an extra visit or urgent lab draw, especially if screening is done earlier, increasing patient burden and potential for scheduling conflicts.",
      "fix": "Allow a wider window (e.g., 7 days) or permit a urine pregnancy test at screening with serum confirmation if positive."
    },
    {
      "title": "Discontinuation visit burden not detailed",
      "quote": "Patients who permanently discontinue from study drug and who opt to withdraw from the study will be asked to complete final study assessments (eg, EOT1 or EOT2).",
      "page": 42,
      "section": "8.3.7 Clinical Assessments Following Study Drug Discontinuation",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The final study assessments (EOT1 or EOT2) are not described in the Schedule of Activities, so sites may not know which procedures are required, potentially leading to incomplete data or extra visits.",
      "fix": "Add a detailed EOT visit to the Schedule of Activities with all required procedures."
    }
  ]
}
